Common result states

What the status is telling you.

✓

High confidence

Evidence is close and consistent. Still inspect unfamiliar locations before saving.

!

Review

Look for a clock offset, one-sided evidence, a sparse route, movement, or disagreement between sources.

—

No suggestion

Open the details to see the nearest GPX boundaries and iPhone photo time gaps. Widen a limit only when the trip makes that safe.

Before reporting a problem

Keep the evidence that explains the run.

  1. Note the iOS version and deviceBackground behavior differs between iOS 17–25 and iOS 26 or later.
  2. Record the camera make and modelLensPin selects candidate photos by exact EXIF camera identity.
  3. Describe the evidence sourceSay whether the run used GPX, nearby iPhone photos, or both—and whether a clock offset was applied.
  4. Keep the completion counts or failure reasonAdded, failed, skipped, album warnings, and EXIF fallbacks describe different outcomes.
Protect private data.

Do not send a full photo library, private GPX route, or precise home coordinates when a filename, time gap, status label, and redacted screenshot are enough.
